dedupe_keys.name: netascore network assessment score toolbox bikeability and walkability

description: NetAScore, the Network Assessment Score toolbox for sustainable mobility, computes bikeability, walkability and related indicators for each street segment from public network data. It was developed at the University of Salzburg by Christian Werner, Martin Loidl and co-authors and introduced in Environment and Planning B in 2024, with separate open-access papers on the bikeability method and on a street-level walkability index and their evaluation studies. It takes OpenStreetMap data for global coverage, or the Austrian authoritative GIP network within Austria, derives attributes and indicators, and exports results as a GeoPackage to view in QGIS. A ready-made Docker image runs the workflow for Salzburg as an example; other areas are set by place name, and settings allow custom indicator weights. Example outputs are on Zenodo. Coverage: any area with OpenStreetMap data. Format and access: Python code, a Docker image and a wiki on GitHub. Licence and cost: MIT, free. Caveats: indices reflect infrastructure suitability, not demand or safety records, and OSM attribute completeness varies. It supports network assessment and capacity planning for walking and cycling infrastructure. It complements BikeDNA and the PeopleForBikes network analysis in the catalogue.
